module_title: Programming Languages - Foundational Basics (High-level vs. Low-level)
introduction: A computer only understands electronic signals represented by 0s and 1s. Programming languages act as a bridge, allowing humans to give instructions to the computer. At this foundational level, we will classify languages based on how close they are to the machine versus how close they are to human language.

core_concepts.title: Low-Level Language (LLL)
core_concepts.description: Languages that are extremely close to the computer's hardware. They deal directly with memory registers and CPU architecture. Because they are designed for machines, they are highly complex and difficult for humans to read or write. Machine Language is the purest form of LLL.

core_concepts.title: High-Level Language (HLL)
core_concepts.description:
Languages designed specifically for human programmers. They use common English words (like 'print', 'if', 'while') and standard mathematical symbols, making them easy to learn, read, and debug. 
Examples: Python, Java, C++, Ruby.

core_concepts.title: Machine Language (1st Generation)
core_concepts.description: The native tongue of the computer CPU. It consists entirely of Binary Code (a continuous stream of 0s and 1s). The computer understands this instantly without needing any translation.

core_concepts.title: The Need for Translators
core_concepts.description: Because humans write code in High-Level Languages (English words) and computers only understand Machine Language (Binary), we strictly need 'Language Translators' to convert the human code into machine code.

important_entities.name: Binary Code
important_entities.significance: In binary, '0' represents an 'Off' electrical state, and '1' represents an 'On' electrical state. All digital processing relies on this.

important_entities.name: Source Code
important_entities.significance: The original text/program written by a software developer in a High-Level Language before it is translated.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants often assume that a computer directly reads and understands Python or C++ code. False! A CPU can NEVER directly execute high-level code. It must always be translated into binary machine code first.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: High-level languages are closer to Human languages. Low-level languages are closer to the core Logic gates of the machine.

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-1 exams, you will often face 'Find the odd one out' questions. If the options are Python, Java, C++, and Machine Language, the answer is Machine Language because it is the only Low-Level Language.
